extracted_claims.text: As adopted in Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (official text of 13 June 2024), the obligations for high-risk AI systems under Article 6(2) and Annex III were originally scheduled to apply/become enforceable from 2 August 2026.

The Commission's Digital Omnibus on AI proposal (COM(2025)836) proposed linking entry into application of Annex III high-risk rules to the availability of supporting measures (harmonised standards, common specifications, Commission guidelines), with the rules applying 6 months after Commission confirmation for Article 6(2)/Annex III systems and 12 months for Article 6(1)/Annex I systems.

A later Commission document (COM(2026)234) restates the Digital Omnibus proposal: Annex III high-risk rules would start to apply after a 6-month transition period once the Commission confirms sufficient availability of standards, and in any case no later than 2 December 2027, but explicitly states this 'remains under negotiation and is subject to agreement between the European Parliament and the Council.'

On 7 May 2026 the Council and Parliament reached an agreement to adjust the timeline for applying high-risk AI (Annex III) rules by up to 16 months, so that the rules would start to apply once the Commission confirms the needed standards and tools are available.

Multiple secondary/legal-analysis sources state that the Digital Omnibus process resulted in a new application date of 2 December 2027 for standalone high-risk AI systems under Annex III (Article 6(2)).

The Council of the EU gave final approval to the Digital Omnibus simplification package on 29 June 2026, formally pushing the Annex III high-risk compliance deadline from 2 August 2026 to 2 December 2027, with a parallel 12-month extension for Annex I embedded high-risk systems from 2 August 2027 to 2 August 2028.
The Digital Omnibus on AI is described as having entered into force on 27 July 2026, after which the Annex III high-risk regime application date became 2 December 2027.
The 2 December 2027 date for Article 6(2)/Annex III high-risk AI obligations is attributed to a specific enacted instrument, Regulation (EU) 2026/1744.

The shift of the Annex III high-risk compliance deadline to 2 December 2027 is described as still pending formal adoption; until published in the EU Official Journal, 2 August 2026 remains the legally binding date.

Obligations for high-risk AI systems that qualify as high-risk because they are safety components of, or themselves, products covered by Union harmonisation legislation in Annex I (Article 6(1)) apply from 2 August 2028.

Transparency obligations under Article 50 apply from 2 August 2026, with a transitional deadline of 2 December 2026 for providers of systems placed on the market before that date to comply with Article 50(2) marking/detection obligations.
New prohibitions on AI systems generating non-consensual intimate material and child sexual abuse material apply from 2 December 2026.

Prohibited AI practices under Article 5 entered into application on 2 February 2025, while enforcement rules for these prohibitions are not yet fully applicable, leaving limited practical experience with their application.
The EU AI Act (Regulation 2024/1689) entered into force on 1 August 2024 and establishes a tiered compliance timeline with obligations scaling to assessed risk level.

A system is classified as high-risk if it meets either of two independent tests: being a safety component of/itself a product under Annex I Union harmonisation legislation requiring third-party conformity assessment (Article 6(1)), or having an intended purpose within one of the eight use-case areas listed in Annex III (Article 6(2)).
High-risk classification under Annex III covers use-case areas including biometrics, critical infrastructure, education, employment, essential services, and law enforcement, among others.

Under the pre-Digital-Omnibus original Article 6 framework, Article 6 and full high-risk obligations under Title III Chapter 2 were set to become enforceable for Annex III systems, with this later superseded/reported as 2 December 2027 in revised commentary.

report:
# When Do Annex III High-Risk AI Obligations Apply Under the EU AI Act?

## Executive Summary
As originally adopted, obligations for high-risk AI systems under Article 6(2) and Annex III of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 were due to apply from 2 August 2026 (low confidence) ([CSA Research Note](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-deadline-20)). However, the Commission's Digital Omnibus on AI proposal and subsequent EU institutional developments have moved to delay this deadline to no later than 2 December 2027, contingent on confirmation that supporting standards are available (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex COM(2025)836](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A52025PC0836); [EUR-Lex COM(2026)234](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A52026DC0234)). Crucially, sources disagree on whether this change has been formally and legally adopted, making the precise binding application date uncertain as of the available research.

## Key Findings

### Original Statutory Timeline
As adopted in the official text of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (13 June 2024), high-risk obligations under Article 6(2) and Annex III were originally scheduled to apply from 2 August 2026 (low confidence) ([Responsible AI Labs](https://responsibleailabs.ai/knowledge-hub/articles/eu-ai-act-august-2026-compliance); [Jaggaer](https://www.jaggaer.com/blog/eu-ai-act-compliance-deadlines)). The Act entered into force on 1 August 2024, establishing a tiered compliance timeline scaled to risk level (low confidence) ([CSA Research Note](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-deadline-20)).

### The Digital Omnibus Proposal and Revised Timeline
The Commission's Digital Omnibus on AI proposal (COM(2025)836) would link the start of Annex III rules to confirmation that supporting measures—harmonised standards, common specifications, and Commission guidelines—are sufficiently available, with application beginning 6 months after such confirmation for Article 6(2)/Annex III systems (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex COM(2025)836](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A52025PC0836)). A later Commission document, COM(2026)234, restates this approach, specifying that application would begin no later than 2 December 2027 as a backstop, but explicitly notes the proposal "remains under negotiation and is subject to agreement between the European Parliament and the Council" (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex COM(2026)234](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A52026DC0234)).

On 7 May 2026, the Council and Parliament reportedly reached political agreement to adjust the Annex III timeline by up to 16 months, tying application to Commission confirmation of standards availability (medium confidence) ([Consilium](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)). Multiple secondary and legal-analysis sources now describe 2 December 2027 as the resulting application date for standalone Annex III high-risk systems (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation); [artificialintelligenceact.eu](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/high-level-summary); [EU AI Compass](https://euaicompass.com/timeline.html)).

### Related Deadlines
Obligations for Annex I high-risk systems (Article 6(1), safety components of regulated products) apply from 2 August 2028 (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation); [artificialintelligenceact.eu](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/high-level-summary)). Transparency obligations under Article 50 apply from 2 August 2026, with a transitional deadline of 2 December 2026 for certain marking obligations (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-enforcement-start)). New prohibitions on AI-generated non-consensual intimate material and CSAM apply from 2 December 2026 (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-enforcement-start)). Article 5 prohibited practices entered into application on 2 February 2025, though enforcement mechanisms remain incomplete (medium confidence) ([Digital Strategy report](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/library/report-review-prohibitions-and-high-risk-ai)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
There is significant disagreement over the legal status of the December 2027 deadline. One source states the Digital Omnibus package received Council final approval on 29 June 2026 (low confidence, 0.12) ([CSA Research Note - Omnibus](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-eu-ai-act-omnibus-vii-deadline-delay-20260)), and another claims it entered into force on 27 July 2026 (low confidence, 0.12) ([Questa AI](https://www.questa-ai.com/privacy-cafe/eu-ai-act-countdown-is-your-annex-iii-system-ready-for-august-2)), with one source even citing a specific regulation number, 2026/1744 (low confidence, 0.12) ([EU AI Compass](https://euaicompass.com/timeline.html)). However, the Commission's own document COM(2026)234 states the change "remains under negotiation," and another source argues that until published in the Official Journal, 2 August 2026 remains the legally binding date (low confidence, 0.12) ([Jaggaer](https://www.jaggaer.com/blog/eu-ai-act-compliance-deadlines)). These conflicting accounts cannot be reconciled with the available evidence.

## Knowledge Gaps
It remains unclear whether the Digital Omnibus on AI has been formally adopted and published in the Official Journal. The precise criteria the Commission will use to confirm "sufficient availability" of standards, and whether such confirmation has occurred, are unknown. It is also unclear whether application could occur earlier than 2 December 2027 if standards become available sooner, since several sources frame this date as a backstop rather than a fixed deadline. The authenticity of "Regulation (EU) 2026/1744" as a genuinely enacted instrument requires verification.

## Methodology Note
This report was produced by an automated research pipeline: web search, source classification, confidence scores computed from source authority, recency and corroboration, and an automated review against the extracted claims.

source_links.notes: Every link points to a gathered source.

citation_coverage.notes: Virtually all factual statements carry markdown citations consistent with the extracted claims; interpretive/summary sentences without direct citations (e.g., the closing sentence of the executive summary) are supported by citations elsewhere in the same paragraph/section.

hallucination_check.notes: All dates, confidence levels, and figures (2 Aug 2026, 2 Dec 2027, 2 Aug 2028, 2 Dec 2026, 2 Feb 2025, the 29 June 2026 approval claim, the 27 July 2026 entry-into-force claim, and 'Regulation (EU) 2026/1744') trace directly to corresponding claims (claim_001 through claim_014) with matching confidence levels. No invented facts or numbers were found.

contradiction_disclosure.notes: The report includes a dedicated 'Contradictions & Uncertainties' section that accurately surfaces the three known contradictions (final-approval date disputes, the 'remains under negotiation' vs. 'already enacted' conflict, and the Official Journal publication status dispute), matching the ground-truth Known Contradictions list.
